headline: Panic in NYC: Teenager opens fire in Times Square after stabbing
summary: A 17-year-old has been detained by the NYPD after a violent dispute left one man injured and tourists fleeing in terror.
details: A violent confrontation in New York City's Times Square on Thursday left one man injured and sparked widespread panic among tourists and pedestrians.

The incident began around 3:30 PM when a group of people became embroiled in a dispute near West 44th and West 45th Streets. During the clash, a 26-year-old man was stabbed in the neck and rushed to a local hospital, where he is expected to recover.

Shortly after the stabbing, a 17-year-old teenager opened fire toward the group involved in the dispute. The NYPD quickly intervened and took the teenager into custody, though formal charges have not yet been filed.
A second shooting incident was reported shortly after in the area of West 45th Street and Eighth Avenue, though police confirmed that no one was injured in either of the shooting events.
Witnesses described a scene of chaos as people scrambled for safety. Some fled into the Raising Cane's restaurant, while others dove to the floor or hid in a nearby Hershey's store.

One witness, Aidan Spencer, recalled the terror, stating that the sound of the gunshots was so loud it felt as if it were happening right beside him. Other tourists noted the high anxiety caused by the violence occurring in such a major tourist hub.
Police recovered a weapon from the scene and are continuing their investigation. They are currently questioning several other individuals believed to be involved in the initial dispute.

headline_marked: Police HQ [[orders alert over Awami League anniversary]] to prevent clashes
headline: Police HQ orders alert over Awami League anniversary to prevent clashes
summary: Police Headquarters has issued an urgent directive to all units across Bangladesh to remain vigilant ahead of the banned party's June 23 anniversary.
details: Police Headquarters has ordered all units across Bangladesh to take security precautions and remain vigilant before the founding anniversary of the Awami League on June 23.
An urgent message was sent to metropolitan police commissioners and range deputy inspectors general, warning that the party may attempt to raise flags and hold public processions.
Authorities fear these activities could trigger clashes with other political groups, including the National Citizen Party (NCP) and Students Against Discrimination.
The directive also noted that any attempts by law enforcement to disrupt these events could potentially draw public aggression toward police officers.
Police officers stated that the measure is precautionary and based on reports from multiple intelligence agencies.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police confirmed they are on high alert, with security checkpoints and operations ongoing to maintain order.
The Awami League is currently banned from all activities pending trials of its leaders, including Sheikh Hasina, on charges of crimes against humanity.
Police are also preparing for Ashura on the 10th of Muharram alongside the anniversary security measures.
caption:
Police are on high alert across Bangladesh as they brace for potential clashes during the Awami League's anniversary.

Police Headquarters has ordered all units across Bangladesh to take security precautions and remain vigilant before the founding anniversary of the Awami League on June 23.

An urgent message was sent to metropolitan police commissioners and range deputy inspectors general, warning that the party may attempt to raise flags and hold public processions.

Authorities fear these activities could trigger clashes with other political groups, including the National Citizen Party (NCP) and Students Against Discrimination.

The directive also noted that any attempts by law enforcement to disrupt these events could potentially draw public aggression toward police officers.

Police officers stated that the measure is precautionary and based on reports from multiple intelligence agencies.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police confirmed they are on high alert, with security checkpoints and operations ongoing to maintain order.

The Awami League is currently banned from all activities pending trials of its leaders, including Sheikh Hasina, on charges of crimes against humanity.

Police are also preparing for Ashura on the 10th of Muharram alongside the anniversary security measures.

#Bangladesh #PoliceAlert #AwamiLeague #Security #Dhaka #Politics

Source: bdnews24.com, Somoy News, Prothom Alo
